name: Nested Single-Encoder Patient-Mean Balanced Logistic Reference
summary: This simple reference estimates how much PAM50 subtype information is linearly recoverable from patient-mean H&E features alone, excluding all clinical, receptor, RNA, and site variables. Within repeated nested patient-level cross-validation, inner folds select a single foundation encoder, PCA rank, and L2 penalty for class-weighted multinomial logistic regression, benchmarked against majority-class and class-prior null baselines. Parallel site-held-out cross-validation across 19 sites audits institutional confounding, establishing the required linear benchmark and testing broad, partial, or site-confounded predictability.
preprocessing: Exclude all forbidden clinical, immunohistochemistry receptor (er, pr, her2), histological_type, age, stage, RNA-derived, and site variables from predictor matrices; assert zero non-image features before fitting.

Restrict supervised modelling and scoring to the 802 PAM50-labelled patients (excluding the 259 unlabelled patients), pooling multi-slide patients into a single tile-count-weighted patient-mean embedding per encoder so every patient is one row.

Within each inner and outer training fold independently, apply feature-wise z-score standardisation followed by truncated SVD PCA (n_pca <= 256, strictly below inner-fold sample size ~427) and transform held-out patients using training-fold parameters only.

Compute inverse-frequency balanced class weights strictly from training-fold subtype counts (LumA, LumB, Basal, Her2) and fit training-fold majority-class and stratified class-prior null baselines on identical fold assignments.
Retain collection site (19 groups) strictly as an external split-grouping index for the secondary site-held-out cross-validation sensitivity audit.
metrics: Out-of-fold four-class macro-F1 and paired macro-F1 difference versus majority-class and stratified class-prior null baselines with 95% patient-level bootstrap CIs across 3x5 repeated nested CV
Proportion of training class-prior multi-class log-loss (Shannon entropy) explained out-of-fold with 95% patient-level bootstrap CI
Macro and per-class one-vs-rest AUROC (LumA, LumB, Basal, Her2) with 95% patient-level bootstrap CIs
Per-class precision, recall, and F1 for LumA, LumB, Basal, and Her2 with 95% bootstrap CIs versus class-prior chance (explicitly auditing Her2 minority recall and LumA-vs-LumB confusion)
Site-held-out grouped CV (19 collection sites) out-of-fold macro-F1 and paired macro-F1 gain over chance with 95% patient-level bootstrap CI
L-BFGS solver convergence verification rate (gradient tolerance <= 1e-4 before max_iter) and inner-fold encoder selection stability across the 15 outer folds
allowed_conclusions: Entitled to conclude broad predictability, partial predictability, site-confounded predictability, or insufficient evidence among TCGA-BRCA patients using frozen single-encoder patient-mean H&E features alone, determined strictly by whether 95% patient-level bootstrap intervals for macro-F1 gain over chance exclude zero in patient-level nested CV, 19-site grouped CV, and all four subtypes; also defines the A5 simple image-only reference benchmark. Cannot claim incremental value over clinical/receptor variables, causal biology, or external clinical utility.
rationale: With 802 labelled patients, 768 to 2560 features, and 65 Her2 cases, fold-internal PCA with balanced L2 logistic regression curbs overfitting and minority collapse. Nested encoder tuning prevents selection bias and provides the required A5 ruler for judging complex models.
